# The TextFold format (`textfold/doc`, version 0)

A document folded into five levels, from a map of its sections to every word, in a form other programs can read and
write: a reader app, an agent that wants the gist before it spends its context on the whole text, a checker that wants
to know which lines a model wrote and what they rest on.

`python3 -m textfold get <link or file> --json` writes it; `python3 -m textfold get <link> --level key --section 3` writes one level of one
section as Markdown. A running server gives it too, from what is stored and without calling a model:
`GET /api/doc/<id>?lang=<code>`. Version 0 may still change: fields will be added without a new version, and a field renamed or
removed will come with version 1.

A part of a text dragged out of the reader into another app carries its words and a link back to it:
[drag-format.md](drag-format.md).

## The contract

Two kinds of text, never mixed:

- **The author's words.** `full` and `brief` are verbatim: `full` is the unit as written, `brief` some of its own
  sentences, as they stand.
- **A model's words.** `key`, `takeaway` and `topic` are written: `takeaway` is one sentence saying what the unit
  establishes, `key` is the takeaway followed by one sentence of reason, `topic` is a noun phrase copied verbatim from
  inside the takeaway.

Every written line is anchored: `evidence` names the sentences of `full` it rests on, by their place in `sentences`.
`brief` is exactly those sentences. A reader can always unfold a written line into the words it came from, and a
checker can compare the two.

## A document

```json
{
  "format": "textfold/doc",
  "version": 0,
  "id": "2512.23916",
  "lang": "en",
  "title": "Constraint Breeds Generalization: Temporal Dynamics as an Inductive Bias",
  "authors": ["Chen, Xia"],
  "date": "2025-12-30",
  "source": {"kind": "arxiv", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23916", "label": "arXiv:2512.23916v2",
             "snapshot": "", "license": "http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/"},
  "levels": ["topic", "takeaway", "key", "brief", "full"],
  "written": ["topic", "takeaway", "key"],
  "provenance": {"made_with": "TextFold 0.10.0", "exported": "2026-10-09T21:47:46Z", "ai_generated": true,
                 "model": "pi/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "levels_made": "2026-10-04T18:01:53", "local": false},
  "sections": [ ... ],
  "links": [ ... ]
}
```

- `id`: the document's id in TextFold (an arXiv id; `pmc…`, `ppr…`, `biorxiv-…`, `wiki-<lang>-<page>`,
  `gh-<owner>--<repo>`, `web-<host>-<hash>`, `pdf-<file hash>`, `md-…`).
- `lang`: the language of the text and its levels. A translation keeps the original's `evidence`.
- `source`: where the text came from. `kind` is `arxiv`, `europepmc` (PubMed Central and Europe PMC), `biorxiv` or
  `medrxiv`, `wikipedia`, `github`, `web`, `pdf` (a file read by the PDF engine) or `markdown`; `snapshot` is the day a changing page was read; `license` is the
  text's own, when it names one. The levels and translations made from a text stay under the text's license.
- `levels`: coarsest first, as a reader zooms in. `written`: the ones a model wrote.

## Provenance

- `ai_generated` and `model`: the written levels were made by this language model. This is the machine-readable mark
  that text was generated by AI (the EU AI Act, article 50(2)); a program that shows the levels should say so too.
- `levels_made`: when they were written. `made_with`: the program and its version.
- `local`: no model has written the levels yet; the written levels are the author's first sentences, cut to length
  (`ai_generated` is then false).

## A section

```json
{"id": "S3", "num": "3", "title": "Arithmetic Reasoning", "depth": 1,
 "takeaway": "Chain-of-thought prompting with PaLM 540B reaches state of the art on GSM8K arithmetic reasoning",
 "topic": "Chain-of-thought prompting",
 "units": [ ... ]}
```

`depth` is 1 for a top-level section, 2 for its subsections. `takeaway` and `topic` are the section's own, written by
the model; at the topic level a document is a map of its sections' topics.

## A unit

A paragraph, a list item or a figure's or table's caption:

```json
{"id": "S3.p1.1", "kind": "paragraph", "role": "result",
 "full": "Though simple for humans, arithmetic reasoning is a task where ...",
 "sentences": ["Though simple for humans, ...", "Strikingly, chain-of-thought prompting ...", "..."],
 "evidence": [1, 2],
 "brief": ["Strikingly, chain-of-thought prompting ...", "..."],
 "key": "Chain-of-thought prompting with a 540B model rivals finetuned models on arithmetic reasoning. Math word problems ...",
 "takeaway": "Chain-of-thought prompting with a 540B model rivals finetuned models on arithmetic reasoning",
 "topic": "arithmetic reasoning"}
```

- `kind`: `paragraph`, `list item`, `caption` or `abstract`.
- `role`: the unit's part in the argument: `context`, `gap`, `claim`, `method`, `setup`, `result`, `analysis` or
  `limitation`.
- Formulas are written as `$…$` (TeX) in every field.

## Links

```json
{"from": "S3.p1.1", "to": "abstract1.2", "rel": "supports"}
```

How the units' claims bear on each other: `supports`, `builds_on`, `qualifies`, `explains`, and `ref` (the text
points at a figure, a table or another unit).

## Text written to fold

The levels can also be written by the author instead of drawn out afterwards: when every paragraph opens with a
sentence that states its point and reads on its own, the first sentence is the takeaway and the rest is the reason,
and no model call is needed to fold it. TextFold's Claude Code mod asks Claude to write its replies that way
(plugins/textfold). A later version of this format will describe that writing as a convention of its own.
